title: Payment Arrangements — Arrangement Type Entry Schedule
content:
Ridgeline offers six types of Payment Arrangements. Each type admits a placed account only when the account's balance due falls within the type's entry gate and the account's placement stage is one the type lists; each type also sets how long after a broken plan on the same account it may be set up again, and how many broken plans in the last 12 months close it to that account.

## Entry gate and eligible placement stages

| Arrangement type | Lowest balance due (USD) | Highest balance due (USD) | Further entry condition | Eligible placement stages |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Promise-to-Pay Arrangement | 10.00 | 15000.00 | — | Early-Out, Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, Warehouse, Legal Review Placement |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | 150.00 | 25000.00 | — | Early-Out, Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, Warehouse, Legal Review Placement |
| Standard Installment Plan | 600.00 | 50000.00 | — | Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, Warehouse, Legal Review Placement |
| Extended Installment Plan | 2000.00 | 75000.00 | — | Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, Warehouse, Legal Review Placement |
| Long-Term Installment Plan | 5000.00 | 250000.00 | — | Warehouse, Legal Review Placement |
| Hardship Reduced-Payment Plan | 300.00 | 75000.00 | A qualifying hardship hold on the account | Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, Warehouse, Legal Review Placement |

Early-Out Placement accounts may take only the Promise-to-Pay Arrangement and the Short-Term Installment Plan. The Long-Term Installment Plan is open only to Warehouse Placement and Legal Review Placement accounts.

## Broken-plan cooling-off and broken-plan limit

The cooling-off figure is the number of calendar days, after the closing date of the most recent plan on the same account that was cancelled as broken and not reinstated, before this type can be set up again. The broken-plan limit is the number of plans on the same account cancelled as broken in the last 12 months at which this type is no longer offered on that account.

| Arrangement type | Cooling-off (calendar days) | Broken-plan limit (plans in 12 months) |
|---|---|---|
| Promise-to-Pay Arrangement | 0 | 3 |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | 30 | 2 |
| Standard Installment Plan | 30 | 2 |
| Extended Installment Plan | 60 | 2 |
| Long-Term Installment Plan | 60 | 1 |
| Hardship Reduced-Payment Plan | 30 | 2 |

## Reading the schedule

- A type with a broken-plan limit of 1 (the Long-Term Installment Plan) is closed to an account as soon as one plan on that account has been cancelled as broken in the last 12 months; a type with a limit of 3 (the Promise-to-Pay Arrangement) stays open until three such plans are on record.
- A cooling-off figure of 0 means the type sets no waiting period after a broken plan.
- Example (hypothetical): a Secondary Placement account with a balance due of 1800.00 sits inside the entry gates of the Promise-to-Pay Arrangement, the Short-Term Installment Plan and the Standard Installment Plan, within the balance range of the Hardship Reduced-Payment Plan (which further requires a qualifying hardship hold on the account), and below the lowest balance due of the Extended and Long-Term Installment Plans; the Long-Term Installment Plan also does not list Secondary Placement.
